evidence.intree_statement: Class EnrichedFunctor (K : Category) `{@Monoidal K} (C : Enriched K) (D : Enriched K) := { efobj : C → D; efmap {x y} : (x ⟿ y) ~{K}~> (efobj x ⟿ efobj y); efmap_id : ∀ x, efmap ∘ eid << I ~~> (efobj x ⟿ efobj x) >> eid; efmap_comp : ∀ x y z, ecompose ∘ efmap ⨂ efmap << (y ⟿ z) ⨂ (x ⟿ y) ~~> (efobj x ⟿ efobj z) >> efmap ∘ ecompose }

Theorem EnrichedFunctor_Two_monotone (P Q : TwoPreorder) : EnrichedFunctor _2 (snd Enriched_Two_preorder P) (snd Enriched_Two_preorder Q) ↔ MonotoneMap P Q. Proof. split; intro X. - destruct X as [f fm _ _]; ... unshelve refine {| mono_map := f |}; intros x y l; apply ehom_of_le_sound; specialize (fm x y); rewrite (ehom_of_le_complete l) in fm; exact fm. - ... (efmap by cases on tpre_dec; the two preservation laws by two_thin). Defined.  — at the book's own base V = Bool the class provably collapses to exactly Def 2.69's data: a function on objects plus the single inequality X(x1,x2) ≤ Y(F x1, F x2)

Theorem Functor_is_Enriched_over_Set (C D : Category) : EnrichedFunctor Sets (snd Category_is_Enriched_over_Set C) (snd Category_is_Enriched_over_Set D) ↔ (C ⟶ D).  — the sanity check that the class is the standard notion: at V = Sets an enriched functor is exactly an ordinary functor, efobj/efmap/efmap_id/efmap_comp unfolding to fobj/fmap/fmap_id/fmap_comp

statement_record.book: For V-categories X and Y, a V-functor F : X → Y consists of ONE constituent — a function F : Ob(X) → Ob(Y) — subject to ONE constraint: for all x1, x2 ∈ Ob(X), X(x1, x2) ≤ Y(F x1, F x2) in V. Because the base is a preorder there is no further data and no equations to impose.
statement_record.intree: Class EnrichedFunctor (K : Category) `{@Monoidal K} (C D : Enriched K) := { efobj : C → D; efmap {x y} : (x ⟿ y) ~{K}~> (efobj x ⟿ efobj y); efmap_id : ∀ x, efmap ∘ eid ≈ eid; efmap_comp : ∀ x y z, ecompose ∘ efmap ⨂ efmap ≈ efmap ∘ ecompose }
statement_record.strength_comparison: same at the book's generality; intree-stronger in base generality. `efobj : C → D` is the book's single constituent and `efmap : (x ⟿ y) ~{K}~> (efobj x ⟿ efobj y)` is verbatim its single constraint (in a thin base a hom IS the relation ≤, so the K-morphism IS the inequality). The class additionally demands the two Kelly coherence equations `efmap_id`/`efmap_comp`, which Def 2.69 never states — but over a preorder base they are vacuous, and Construction/Enriched/Two.v discharges both by `apply two_thin` (Instance/Two/Monoidal.v:26, `two_thin : ∀ (f g : TwoHom x y), f = g`), so no extra hypothesis is imposed in the book's setting; over a general proof-relevant base they are the correct definition. Two disclosures, neither an actionable gap for this item. (1) `EnrichedFunctor_Two_monotone` is stated for enrichments in the IMAGE of `Enriched_of_TwoPreorder` (`snd Enriched_Two_preorder P`) rather than for arbitrary Bool-categories, matching the book's own framing but inheriting the Ex 2.50 round-trip gap. (2) The library has no `MonoidalPreorder` class and no generic bridge from a symmetric monoidal preorder to a thin monoidal category, so a base must be hand-built; exactly one preorder base exists in tree (`Two_Monoidal`, Instance/Two/Monoidal.v:105). The surrounding API the book will need is present: `EnrichedId`/`EnrichedCompose` (Construction/Enriched/Compose.v:25,49) and the V-functor category `Enriched_Fun C D` (Construction/Enriched/Fun.v:270).

evidence.intree_statement: Theorem EnrichedFunctor_Two_monotone (P Q : TwoPreorder) : EnrichedFunctor _2 (snd Enriched_Two_preorder P) (snd Enriched_Two_preorder Q) ↔ MonotoneMap P Q.  — proved in BOTH directions: forward, `mono_map := f` with monotonicity `ehom_of_le_sound` applied to `efmap` after `rewrite (ehom_of_le_complete l)`; backward, `efmap` by cases on `tpre_dec P x y` (top-to-top from `mono_le`, else `two_bot`) with `efmap_id`/`efmap_comp` discharged by `two_thin`

Record MonotoneMap (P Q : TwoPreorder) := { mono_map : tpre_carrier P → tpre_carrier Q; mono_le x y : tpre_le P x y → tpre_le Q (mono_map x) (mono_map y) }  — the book's 'monotone map' side of the identification, exactly a function plus the implication x1 ≤ x2 → F x1 ≤ F x2

statement_record.book: Taking V = Bool, so that preorders are Bool-categories with X(x1,x2) = true written x1 ≤ x2, the V-functors of Def 2.69 are exactly the monotone maps: a function F : X → Y satisfying X(x1,x2) ≤ Y(F x1, F x2) in Bool is precisely one with x1 ≤_X x2 implying F x1 ≤_Y F x2.
statement_record.intree: Theorem EnrichedFunctor_Two_monotone (P Q : TwoPreorder) : EnrichedFunctor _2 (snd Enriched_Two_preorder P) (snd Enriched_Two_preorder Q) ↔ MonotoneMap P Q, with MonotoneMap := { mono_map : tpre_carrier P → tpre_carrier Q; mono_le x y : tpre_le P x y → tpre_le Q (mono_map x) (mono_map y) }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same in substance, both directions machine-checked, at the genuine base Bool (`Two_Monoidal` has tensor := `two_meet` = AND and unit := `TwoY` = true, Instance/Two/Monoidal.v:37,105). Three disclosures. (1) `↔` is `iffT` (Lib/Foundation.v:72), a pair of maps carrying no inverse laws, so 'exactly' is asserted only as mutual constructibility, not as a bijection of the two types — the same weakening recorded at Ex 2.50. (2) The theorem quantifies over enrichments of the form `snd Enriched_Two_preorder P` (i.e. built from a preorder by `Enriched_of_TwoPreorder`) rather than over arbitrary `Enriched _2 Two_Monoidal`; this matches the book, which also views preorders qua Bool-categories, but a fully general form would need the Ex 2.50 round trip. (3) `TwoPreorder` (Construction/Enriched/Two.v:60) carries a decidability field `tpre_dec x y : tpre_le x y + (tpre_le x y → False)` that the classical statement does not, the unavoidable constructive price of computing a truth value; the file header discloses it, and the converse direction supplies decidability for free.

statement_record.book: The correspondence of Thm 2.49 together with Example 2.70 is in fact an EQUIVALENCE of categories between the category of preorders (with monotone maps) and the category of Bool-categories (with Bool-functors); the vocabulary needed to state this precisely is developed in the next chapter (Remark 3.59).
statement_record.intree: Theorem Enriched_Two_preorder : @Enriched _2 Two_Monoidal ↔ TwoPreorder (object level) and Theorem EnrichedFunctor_Two_monotone (P Q : TwoPreorder) : EnrichedFunctor _2 (snd Enriched_Two_preorder P) (snd Enriched_Two_preorder Q) ↔ MonotoneMap P Q (hom level).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: both LEGS of the correspondence exist, but the correspondence is never assembled into anything categorical. `↔` is `iffT` (Lib/Foundation.v:72), a bare pair of maps with no inverse laws, no functoriality (nothing says the object map and the hom map respect identities and composition), and no naturality; and there are no CATEGORIES for the equivalence to live between. So the in-tree content is 'maps both ways on objects, and maps both ways on homs, for each fixed pair', strictly weaker than 'an equivalence of categories'. The general machinery to state the conclusion does exist and is unused here (Theory/Equivalence.v's quasi-inverse `Equivalence` class, the Full+Faithful+essentially-surjective characterization in Theory/Equivalence/FullFaithful.v, and `≅[Cat]` over Instance/Cat.v).

gap: Three precise omissions. (1) NO CATEGORY OF PREORDERS. Instance/Proset.v:33 `Proset P` and Instance/Poset.v:116 `Poset P` build a SINGLE preorder AS a category; nothing has preorders as its objects and monotone maps as its morphisms (`grep -rn -E 'Definition (Pos|Preord|Prosets|Posets|POS)' .` : 0 hits, and both files' headers point at an 'Ord'/'Pos' they do not construct — Instance/Proset.v:20 'See also [Ord], for the category of preordered sets', Instance/Poset.v:21-22 'See also [Pos] ... whose objects are posets'). `MonotoneMap` (Construction/Enriched/Two.v:175) supplies the hom type but no `Category` instance is built from it. (2) NO CATEGORY OF Bool-CATEGORIES. Construction/Enriched/Fun.v:270 builds only `Enriched_Fun C D`, the ordinary category of V-functors between two FIXED V-categories; there is no `V-Cat` whose objects are the V-categories (`grep -rn -E 'VCat|ECat|EnrichedCat|Enriched_Cat' .` : 0 hits), even though the 1-cell structure needed for it is present (`EnrichedId`, `EnrichedCompose`, Construction/Enriched/Compose.v:25,49). (3) CONSEQUENTLY NO FUNCTORS AND NO EQUIVALENCE. Since neither category exists, neither direction is a functor and no `Equivalence`/`≅[Cat]`/`Isomorphism` instance relates them; nothing in tree even asserts the underlying BIJECTION (that is the separately-recorded PARTIAL at 7sketches:2.3.2:ex50, whose round trips are likewise unstated), so full-faithfulness and essential surjectivity — the content of 'equivalence' — are entirely absent.
